text: Git branching is an important part of version control. A branch lets you work on new ideas without changing the main code. Developers often create feature branches to add new features or fix bugs safely. When the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main branch. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the changes. This workflow keeps the project organized and reduces mistakes. If something goes wrong, you can simply go back to an earlier version. Learning how branches, merging, and pull requests work together helps you collaborate better with your team.
